ablation_behavior_off: Shuffle item-to-row association of the frozen transition and co-consumption signals, recompute cached barycenters/gates/negative lists under that shuffled association, and keep the hyperbolic scorer and coefficients fixed.
ablation_both_on: Use correctly indexed train-only incoming transitions and co-consumption hard negatives with Poincare barycenters/distances at -0.1; no extra collision alphabet or Stage3 change.
ablation_geometry_off: Replace Frechet barycenters by weighted Euclidean means and all geodesic distances by squared Euclidean distances, with same behavior, cache size, coefficients, candidate sampler and initialization.
behavior_computation: Within each training user's chronological training events, count adjacent predecessor->target pairs n_pi. Normalize incoming predecessor counts per target, aggregate predecessor code-region probabilities into p(region|i), and compute normalized entropy. Separately compute binary-user-set co-consumption cosine and choose a top-20 neighbor r with no observed predecessor edge into i; freeze the sparse counts and negative candidate lists.
behavior_signal: Directed incoming transition context and co-consumption-similar non-transition hard negatives, both derived from training interactions.
cost_estimate: One sparse transition/count pass and per-item top predecessor cache. Per step sample B targets and at most one hard negative each; barycenter evaluation can use at most 8 cached predecessor representatives, costing O(16BD+BKD) with 8-step Karcher iterations, versus O(BKD) baseline. At frozen scale 72,000 optimizer steps, this is at most 72,000*B*16D extra barycenter coordinate updates plus the existing candidate scoring; cache final detached barycenters per epoch to reduce to O(BKD+BD) while refreshing on 24 steps/epoch. Expected moderate overhead, fixed four tokens.
coupling_equation: S(i,k)=g_i[d_{-0.1}(v_k,b_i)^2-eta*d_{-0.1}(v_k,b_{r(i)})^2]+(1-g_i)d_{-0.1}(v_k,z_i)^2, with b_i=FrechetMean_{p}(n_{pi}/n_i, v_{a_p}) and r(i) selected by train co-consumption similarity subject to n_{r,i}=0.
coupling_path: Train transitions determine predecessor-region weights and concentration gate; co-consumption identifies a hard negative; both barycenters are formed in the Poincare ball and their geodesic distances change each first-token candidate's assignment probability.

evidence_revision.evidence_note: Positive row scalar leaves every arg-min unchanged: True; codeword-dependent weight moved 0 of the top-1
evidence_revision.revision: Withdraw the claim that the proposed behavior-dependent weighting can move assignments: the measured positive row scalar leaves every arg-min unchanged, and the codeword-dependent weight moved 0 of the top-1 assignments, so the evidence does not establish that the proposed score changes assignments
evidence_revision.withdrawn: The claim that this proposal's behavior-dependent weighting or codeword-dependent weighting changes top-1 assignment behavior

falsifiable_hypothesis: Concentrated incoming context is a useful supervision target: items whose predecessors come from fewer distinct regions should be pulled toward their incoming hyperbolic barycenter, while co-consumption-close non-transition items are pushed away. Keep only if concentration-stratified gold-prefix survival and the discrimination gap improve without harming diffuse-target recall, and both-on Stage3 test_R@10 exceeds 0.065 and both controls.
hyperbolic_location: First-level code candidate score and soft assignment in Stage2; the incoming-context barycenter and negative-context barycenter are directly compared to candidate prototypes before argmin/softmax.
hyperbolic_operator: Poincare Frechet/Karcher weighted barycenter and squared Poincare geodesic distance at fixed curvature -0.1; barycenter iterations use log maps to the current iterate and exp map back.
key_change: Precompute each item's sparse predecessor-region distribution from training transitions, represent the distribution by a weighted Poincare Fréchet barycenter of predecessor first-token prototypes, and include positive-versus-hard-negative geodesic contrast in the first-token candidate score. Optimize sampled candidate comparisons only; no new extension tokens.
leakage_boundary: Use only training users/events and training timestamps when building n and co-consumption; no validation/test interactions, future events, or prediction-time context enter barycenters or SIDs. Current predecessor assignments are model states trained only on those frozen edges.
motivation: A next item reached from many distinct prior regions is difficult to tokenize; its first-level region should inherit the concentrated incoming context that best explains its observed predecessors, without collapsing merely similar but behaviorally wrong items together.
novelty: Use each candidate first-token prototype as a hyperbolic destination and a train-only incoming predecessor-context barycenter as its target, while a co-consumption-hard negative destination supplies explicit rejection pressure. This is not a successor-consensus term added to Euclidean assignment: predecessor concentration and the negative contrast jointly alter the actual curved candidate assignment score.
observables: Expect target assignment concentration by incoming-region entropy bin, higher positive-minus-negative gap, improved cooccur_overlap_L3 and adjacency_L3, and changes in L1 Hard ER and gold-prefix survival depths 1-4. Report extension alphabet and frozen Stage3 test_R@10 alongside all required measures.
risks: Early assignments make predecessor regions noisy; cached barycenters can stale; entropy gating can suppress useful learning for rare items; incoming context may not align with next-item ranking, and hard negatives can include unobserved transitions.
safeguards: Smooth incoming counts; fall back to encoder point for no predecessors; renormalize top-M weights; clamp ball norms below (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c), stable log/exp maps and float32, stop gradients through stale cached context, refresh cache once per epoch, mask invalid negatives and skip empty cases. Clip gradients and bound eta/g_i to [0,1]. Keep all sparse data structures train-only; never materialize dense item-item matrices.
spec_equations: p_i(p)=n_{pi}/(sum_q n_{qi}+eps); q_p(k)=softmax(-d_c(v_k,z_p)^2/tau_q); r_i(k)=sum_p p_i(p)*stopgrad(q_p(k)); H_i=-sum_k r_i(k)log(r_i(k)+eps)/log(max(2,K)); g_i=clip(1-H_i,0,1). For top M=8 predecessors, b_i initialized at highest-weight prototype and repeat 8 times: u=sum_p p_i(p)log_{b}(v_{a_p}); b=exp_b(u), renormalizing weights over retained predecessors. Select r(i)=argmax cooc_cos(i,r) subject to no train edge r->i. Compute S(i,k) as in COUPLING EQUATION; q_i=softmax(-S(i,:)/tau), use straight-through argmax; add standard RQ-VAE reconstruction and commitment/codebook losses. Compute negative b_r identically. A detach assignment probabilities in barycenter construction each epoch; gradients flow through candidate distances and assignment only.
spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are train-only sparse directed transition counts, train co-consumption nearest-neighbor lists, item IDs, first-token prototypes/assignments, encoder latents, c=-0.1, M=8, Karcher iterations=8, eta and temperature. Outputs are per-item cached behavior barycenters/gates, first-token candidate scores/probabilities, and unchanged downstream residual tokens.

specification.text: Build directed counts n_{pi} from adjacent training events. During a minibatch, get the current soft first-token probabilities q_p over K prototypes and compute for target i a cached sparse weighted prototype barycenter b_i=FrechetMean_{p:n_pi>0}(prototype[p], normalized n_pi). For each target, select positive target-side context i and hard negative item r with high training co-consumption cosine but no transition into i. Score candidate code k by S(i,k)=d_c(v_k,b_i)^2 - eta*d_c(v_k,b_r)^2, where b_r is r's incoming-context barycenter; use softmax(-S/tau) for straight-through assignment, plus standard reconstruction/VQ losses. Downweight targets with diffuse predecessor-region distribution using g_i=1-H(p(region|i))/log(max(2,K)), clipped [0,1], so the actual score is S_g=g_i*S+(1-g_i)*S_base-curved; compute g from train counts and current predecessor assignments detached. Curved distance and behavior both enter each candidate score.

title: Incoming-context hyperbolic barycenter assignment with rejection pressure
